source.title: Weight Decay Improves Language Model Plasticity
source.authors: Tessa Han; Sebastian Bordt; Hanlin Zhang; S. Kakade

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. Some figure text is flattened, but the relevant correlation coefficients are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether pretraining validation loss predicts downstream performance, using correlations and fine-tuning outcomes rather than reproducing the original scaling-law measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper does not sweep model size, tokens, or compute to test power laws, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, or architecture effects. Its own measurements of pretraining loss versus downstream performance bear on V6. Weight-decay effects on plasticity and the reported probing, attention-rank, and train-validation-gap results do not test the other listed versions.
record.test_reason: Within each fixed model size and token budget, the study varies only pretraining weight decay. It then correlates pretraining validation loss with accuracy after fine-tuning on six CoT tasks (Fig. 3, Fig. 9, Fig. 10, Fig. 20). It argues that loss is not a reliable proxy for downstream performance, which bears on the loss-based half of V6. It does not sweep scale, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say better pretraining loss tends to correlate with better downstream performance but is not a perfect proxy. Models with similar loss can differ downstream, and lower-loss models can do worse after fine-tuning (notably OLMo-2-1B-140x). They call the correlations suggestive given n ≤ 10. They also say the main takeaway does not depend on the correlations, and that selecting pretraining hyperparameters on loss alone can miss the best fine-tuned model.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies weight-decay effects on plasticity and the association between pretraining loss and downstream fine-tuning results; it does not fit or extrapolate scaling laws or estimate compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlation strength and sign vary across model groups and evaluation metrics; the reported leave-one-out correlations also vary in magnitude and sign.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 306 (2026)
record.problems: The authors note small samples for correlations (n ≤ 10 per model group) and that leave-one-out correlations can change in magnitude and sign. Correlation results are presented in figures rather than a numerical results table.
record.rows_left_out: No results bearing on V6 were left out. The paper's weight-decay plasticity results and mechanistic measurements were not included because they do not test the listed scaling-law claim versions.

untested.parts: No sweep of parameters, tokens or compute; no power-law loss fit.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No compute-optimal allocation. 20 TPP is taken from Hoffmann et al. as a setting, not tested.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
No power-law form tested in other modalities or regimes. Fine-tuning is used, but not as a scaling law.
Predictability with scale is untested. Loss varies only through weight decay at fixed size, and downstream means post-fine-tuning accuracy. No functional predictive law is fitted.
No fitted exponents and no comparison of fitting choices.

missing.what: Correct Ratio@16 and ORM(avg@16) loss–accuracy correlations for the six-task average. ORM appears to be r = -0.68, -0.96, -0.97, -0.91, 0.27, but the flattened text makes the panel mapping uncertain.
Per-task loss–accuracy correlations for each of the six CoT datasets. Several are positive for 20 TPP groups.
Learning-rate × weight-decay sweep for OLMo-2-1B-20x. The model with the best pretraining loss is not the best after fine-tuning.
Upstream benchmark accuracy of the base models follows loss order, e.g. OLMo-140x gets 0.61/0.60/0.56 at wd 0.1/0.3/1.0.
Explicit example: OLMo-2-1B-140x losses of 2.6088 (wd 0.1) vs 2.6208/2.7064 (wd 0.3/1.0), with the higher-loss models better after fine-tuning.

record.verdict_notes: Loss differences arise only from weight decay at fixed size and token count, so this bears on loss-as-proxy, not on scale-driven predictability. Downstream means after SFT. Changes from the record: tranche is T5 rather than T2, because the study argues the loss-proxy view is partial. The record wrongly put r3 and r4 (strong correlations) under limits_scope; they move to supports. Small group sizes (n=3 for the 4B group, n=4 for the 140x group) weaken both the supports and challenges verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Power-law loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of power-law fits from smaller to larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation trends.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as settings for the claimed power-law form.

Predictability with scale is not tested. The study tests association between pretraining loss and post-fine-tuning performance for the reported models and CoT tasks, not a general predictive law across downstream tasks.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices, and bending of scaling curves.

rows.subject: Five model groups pooled
rows.stage_stated: pretrained variants, then fine-tuned on CoT tasks
rows.operation_detail: Leave-one-out stability analysis of correlations between pretraining loss and fine-tuning performance.
rows.measure: Stability of Pearson correlation coefficients
rows.value: Correlations can change noticeably in magnitude and sign.
rows.note: The authors say this instability further supports that pretraining loss is not perfectly predictive of fine-tuning accuracy.
rows.check: This is a leave-one-out stability analysis with no legible values (Fig. 10). It shows the correlations are unstable but gives no rate or strength, so 'partial' cannot be read from it.

relationships.condition: 20 TPP groups Llama-2-1B, Llama-2-4B and OLMo-2-1B-20x on the averaged CoT metrics (one exception: Llama-2-1B Greedy, see limits_scope)
relationships.reason: Lower pretraining loss goes with higher post-fine-tuning accuracy, r between -0.75 and -1.00 (r3, r4, r7, r8, r9, r12, r13, r14, r17, r18, r19). The 4B group has only n=3.
relationships.display_finding: Pretraining loss correlates negatively with post-fine-tuning accuracy at r=−0.75 to −1.00, although the 4B group contains only three observations.

relationships.reason: Correlations are weak or near zero: r = -0.10, -0.32, -0.17, -0.45 (r1, r2, r11, r16). Loss predicts poorly here.
relationships.display_finding: Loss–performance correlations were weak or near zero at −0.10, −0.32, −0.17 and −0.45.

relationships.condition: Overtrained OLMo-2-1B-140x on all four metrics; Llama-2-0.5B-20x on Pass@16
relationships.reason: Correlations are positive (r = 0.24–0.38, r5, r10, r15, r20; r = 0.28, r6), so lower loss goes with worse downstream accuracy. Text example: wd 0.1 has the lowest loss but worse fine-tuned accuracy. n=4 for the 140x group.
relationships.display_finding: Loss–accuracy correlations were positive for OLMo-2-1B-140x across four metrics (r = 0.24–0.38; n = 4) and Llama-2-0.5B-20x on Pass@16 (r = 0.28), and weight decay 0.1 produced the lowest loss but worse fine-tuned accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Strong negative correlations for Pass@16, Maj@16, and RM@16 in Llama-2-1B-20x, Llama-2-4B-20x, and OLMo-2-1B-20x
reader_labels.reason: These correlations associate lower pretraining loss with higher downstream accuracy in the tested conditions (r7-r9, r12-r14, r17-r19).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Correlation results across the tested groups and metrics
reader_labels.reason: Some relationships are weak, and the leave-one-out analysis shows that the correlation can vary in magnitude and sign (r1-r4, r6, r11, r16, r21).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Greedy, Pass@16, and Maj@16 results for OLMo-2-1B-140x; Pass@16 for Llama-2-0.5B-20x
reader_labels.reason: The positive correlations run opposite to the expected association of lower pretraining loss with better downstream accuracy (r5, r6, r10, r15, r20).
